problemStatement.formal: For a nonnegative rational-valued function on a nonempty finite set and 0 <= theta < 1, prove the quantitative Paley-Zygmund lower bound in counting and probability form.
problemStatement.plain: Strengthen the second moment method with a threshold parameter: many points must exceed a fixed fraction of the mean when the second moment is controlled.
whyMatters: Paley-Zygmund is a standard quantitative upgrade of the second moment method.
The threshold form is useful in probabilistic combinatorics because it lower-bounds not just existence but prevalence.
The finite rational proof gives a concrete, Lean-checkable version of the common textbook inequality.

proven: A finite-sum Cauchy-Schwarz lemma is proved for rational-valued functions on a Finset.
The counting-form quantitative Paley-Zygmund inequality is proved for nonnegative f and 0 <= theta < 1 (Lean: paley_zygmund_quantitative).
A probability-form corollary divides by the second moment when the squared-sum term is positive (Lean: paley_zygmund_probability).
The theta = 0 specialization recovers the positive-support lower bound used by the qualitative second moment method (Lean: paley_zygmund_at_zero).
knownResults.goal: Expose the verified finite quantitative Paley-Zygmund inequality and its second-moment-method corollaries.

insights: The quantitative Paley-Zygmund inequality with threshold θ follows from Cauchy-Schwarz on the above-threshold subset plus a sum decomposition argument
The proof uses sq_sum_le (Cauchy-Schwarz for finite sums), Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not, and Finset.sum_le_sum for the below-threshold bound
At θ=0, the quantitative PZ gives (∑f)² ≤ |{f>0}| · ∑f², strictly stronger than the qualitative P[X>0]>0
